add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.texto: WHAT: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances and call write(rBigInteger)/write(sBigInteger) but discard the results, then lines 117-121 rebuild the same encoders to produce the actual return value. WHY: the discarded work is a copy-paste artifact that adds confusion and wasted allocation on the signing hot path without affecting output. HOW: remove the two dead statements at lines 114-115, keeping only the writeDerSeq(...).toByteArray() expression that actually returns.

add-caching-support-for-identityprovider.texto: WHAT: The new getForLogin only guards with `isInvalid(cacheKey)` and never consults `isInvalid(organizationId)`, unlike getByOrganization which checks `isInvalid(cacheKey) || isInvalid(orgId)` (line 173). WHY: Organization removal/change calls registerOrganizationInvalidation, which registers the plain orgId invalidation (`realmCache.registerInvalidation(id)`, InfinispanOrganizationProvider line 304) but NOT cacheKeyForLogin; with the login cache keyed only by (realm, mode), a cached getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, orgId) for a since-deleted or changed org keeps returning the stale internal-ID set for that searchKey. HOW: add the org-scoped check to the guard, e.g. `if (isInvalid(cacheKey) || (organizationId != null && isInvalid(organizationId)))`.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.texto: WHAT: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) only evaluates the per-client resource (with an all-clients fallback limited to existing policies) and never honors the canManage/canConfigure transitive grant described in the ClientPermissionEvaluator contract. WHY: because the MANAGE branch is checked first, a caller granted MANAGE on a single client makes canView(client) short-circuit to true at line 78 without any VIEW grant, and canMapRoles(client) returns false for an admin granted only the all-clients MANAGE permission. HOW: add the transitive checks, e.g. in canMapRoles return `canManage(client) || hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES)` and in canView(client) gate the MANAGE/VIEW short-circuit consistently with canConfigure.

WHAT: the ClientRemovedEvent branch now calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false), but MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193-195). WHY: with the AdminFineGrainedAuthzV2 feature enabled, deleting a client fires ClientRemovedEvent and the listener throws an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException inside the provider-event dispatcher, breaking client deletion. HOW: skip the call for the V2 evaluator (e.g. check the feature/evaluator type) or implement the V2 no-op/cleanup instead of throwing.

WHAT: getClientsWithPermission iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`, but per-client resources are created without a resource type in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (`resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` never calls `setType`), so only the single "all-clients" resource carries type "Clients". WHY: the method always returns an empty set for clients, so callers relying on it to enumerate clients a subject has a scope for get no results (users with a per-client CLIENTS permission are never reported), silently breaking the client resource-type feature this PR adds. HOW: set the resource type when creating the per-client resource (e.g. `resource.setType(resourceType)` after `resourceStore.create(...)` in getOrCreateResource), consistent with the all-clients resource created via `resource.setType(type)`.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.texto: WHAT: `EmailValidator#validate_each` (line 13) calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which increments `match_count` and saves, but `UsersController#create` runs validations twice per request (`user.valid?` at users_controller.rb:168, then `user.save` at users_controller.rb:172). WHY: every blocked signup attempt records two matches instead of one, so the new `match_count` statistic the PR exists to track is inflated. HOW: either perform the `BlockedEmail` lookup/increment outside the validation callback (e.g. in the controller before/after the single save), or make the increment idempotent within a request (memoize the match per email).

WHAT: `should_block?` does a read-modify-write on `match_count` (`record.match_count += 1; record.save`) without a lock or atomic SQL update. WHY: two concurrent signup attempts for the same blocked email both read the same count and the later save overwrites the earlier one, losing an increment and producing an inaccurate match count. HOW: use `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` (or `record.increment!`/`update_column` with an atomic counter) instead of in-memory `+= 1` then `save`.

WHAT: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` (line 17) sets the array on the controller prototype, so a single array instance is shared by every `Discourse.CreateAccountController` instance. WHY: emails rejected in one signup-modal session persist into later sessions (and into any other instance), causing stale `emailValidation` failures that block the user even for a fresh attempt. HOW: make the array per-instance, e.g. initialize it in `init()` (`this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A())`) rather than as a class property.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.texto: WHAT: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds `groupResource.getId()` (the authorization ResourceEntity primary key) to the returned set instead of the group id. WHY: UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource store this set in the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute, and JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery (JpaUserProvider.java:1070) matches it as `UserGroupMembershipEntity.groupId IN (groupIds)` — resource ids never equal group ids, so a V2 admin with VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on a group sees an empty user list and a count of 0, silently breaking the feature. HOW: Derive the group id from the resource name (the V2 group resource is created with name = groupId), e.g. add `groupResource.getName()` (or strip the `group.resource.` prefix) instead of `groupResource.getId()`; mirror V1 GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission.

WHAT: `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE /* "Groups" */, ...)` returns no per-group resources because per-group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource never call `resource.setType(...)` — only the type-level all-groups resource gets `setType(type)` (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:274). WHY: The callback is therefore never invoked for individual group resources, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission stays empty even when the caller holds VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on specific groups; V1 avoids this by using `setType("Group")` (GroupPermissions.java:117) and `findByType(server, "Group", ...)`. HOW: Look up per-group resources by name (`resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`) or assign/query the correct resource type consistently with how the resources are created.

WHAT: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission invokes hasPermission (i.e. root.evaluatePermission) once for every Groups-type resource via the findByType callback. WHY: On the user-list and user-count endpoints this runs a full authorization evaluation per group in the realm, turning a single request into O(N) policy evaluations for realms with many groups. HOW: Evaluate the all-groups resource once and short-circuit, and/or batch the per-group permission resolution instead of one evaluatePermission call per resource.

WHAT: getSubGroups replaced `canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g)` with the per-group filter `auth.groups()::canView`, dropping the global fallback. WHY: GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel) returns true only for MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS roles or a permission scoped to that specific group, so an admin granted the all-groups VIEW permission can no longer list subgroups even though canViewGlobal previously let them. HOW: restore the global fallback, e.g. `boolean canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView(); ... .filter(g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g))`.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.texto: WHAT: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, but `isTeamAdmin` already returns truthy for members whose role is ADMIN *or* OWNER, so ANDing with `isTeamOwner` reduces the check to OWNER-only. WHY: A team ADMIN (not OWNER) is rejected with FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's bookings, contradicting the `AdminOrOwner` intent. HOW: replace the `&&` with `||`, or drop the redundant `isTeamOwner` call: `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0);`

WHAT: Guest dedup/blacklist uses a case-sensitive comparison — `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where only the blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` is not. WHY: Existing attendees can be duplicated and blacklisted addresses re-added simply by varying letter case (e.g. `Foo@bar.com` vs `foo@bar.com`), bypassing both the duplicate filter and the blacklist. HOW: normalize both sides to lowercase (as the existing pattern in checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked.ts does), e.g. compare `guest.toLowerCase()` against `attendee.email.toLowerCase()` and the lowercased blacklist.

WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`; in email-manager.ts `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` then decides that any attendee whose email appears in the raw input is a new guest and sends them a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail`. WHY: Re-submitting an already-existing attendee's email (which `uniqueGuests` correctly excludes) causes that existing attendee to receive a full booking email instead of the add-guests notification. HOW: pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, uniqueGuests)`.

WHAT: The handler never checks `booking.status`, so guests can be added to a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking. WHY: A user can call `addGuests` on a cancelled/rejected booking, which permanently mutates `booking.attendees` and fires calendar updates and confirmation emails for a booking that no longer exists. HOW: After fetching the booking, reject unless `booking.status === BookingStatus.ACCEPTED` (or PENDING when guests can be pre-added), throwing a `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST" })`.

add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.texto: WHAT: santizeAnchors walks the translation anchors and the English anchors in lockstep by position and flags any mismatch, so a translation that legitimately reorders the same anchor tags relative to English is reported as an error. WHY: word-order-different locales (e.g. RTL or verb-final languages) commonly move the link, causing a false "Didn't find anchor tag" in ThemeVerifierMojo and failing the whole build for a valid translation. HOW: require only that the multiset of anchor tags in the translation is a subset of the English anchor tags (e.g. compare sorted lists / counts) instead of matching them pairwise by iteration order.

WHAT: the prefix/suffix diff-extraction computes start against value/sanitized and end against value/sanitized independently, with no invariant that start <= value.length() - end, so value.substring(start, value.length() - end) can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. WHY: when the sanitizer output retains overlapping prefix and suffix characters of value (both loops are bounded only by sanitized.length()), start + end can exceed value.length(), crashing the build with an exception instead of reporting the offending key. HOW: clamp end to value.length() - start before building the substrings.

add-rolling-updates-feature-flag-and-com.texto: WHAT: `createInitialDeployment` returns early at line 105 when `updateStrategy == null`, before the new feature block at lines 112-115 that enables `rolling-updates`, so the `null`-strategy parameterizations of `testImageChange` and `testCacheMaxCount` run without the feature enabled. WHY: the PR's own docs (advanced-configuration.adoc) require `rolling-updates` to be enabled or the Operator fails, and `eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus`/`eventuallyRecreateUpgradeStatus` are asserted on these cases — the null-strategy runs will deploy an un-enabled Keycloak and can fail to reach the expected status. HOW: move the feature-spec block before the `updateStrategy == null` early return so every created deployment enables `rolling-updates`.

createInitialDeployment early-returns when updateStrategy==null before enabling ROLLING_UPDATES, leaving the feature flag disabled for the rolling upgrade path when upgradeStrategy() supplies null and testCacheMaxCount triggers the rolling path. This matches the configuration that causes the Operator to fail according to new documentation.

advanced-date-override-handling-and-time.texto: WHAT: the slot end-minute bound is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so `end` is always identical to `start`. WHY: the `end > workingHour.endTime` guard can never fire, so a slot whose start is inside working hours but which runs past the working-hours end is still treated as available. HOW: compute the end bound from `slotEndTime` (e.g. `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()`).

WHAT: when a slot falls inside a date-override window the function returns `true` at line 133-135 before the `busy.every(...)` conflict check runs. WHY: any existing booking that overlaps a slot covered by a date override is treated as free, so the event can be double-booked on override days. HOW: do not early-return on `dateOverrideExist`; fall through to the busy-conflict check (only the out-of-override branches should return false).

advanced-query-processing-architecture-g.texto: WHAT: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates every target with applyTemplateVariables and then hands those already-interpolated targets to runSplitQuery, which interpolates them a second time (querySplitting.ts:299). WHY: applyTemplateVariables runs addAdHocFilters, and for parsed/non-indexed labels addFilterAsLabelFilter (modifyQuery.ts:511) appends the filter without dedup, so each ad-hoc filter is added twice to the expression (e.g. `... | foo="bar" | foo="bar"`), sending duplicate/incorrect label filters to Loki. HOW: interpolate only once — since runSplitQuery now performs the interpolation, drop the .map(...) here and pass the filtered raw targets (or stop interpolating inside runSplitQuery).

WHAT: runSplitQuery re-applies applyTemplateVariables (and thus addAdHocFilters) to targets that runShardSplitQuery already interpolated at shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 before invoking runSplitQuery at shardQuerySplitting.ts:163, so ad-hoc filters are applied twice to the same target. WHY: addFilterAsLabelFilter (modifyQuery.ts:511-541) appends `| key op \`value\`` without any dedup guard, so a parsed/structured-metadata ad-hoc filter (e.g. `| level="info"`) is duplicated in the emitted LogQL when the shard-splitting path is used, producing redundant/incorrect label filters in each sub-request. HOW: skip the second interpolation for shard sub-requests (e.g. pass an option to runSplitQuery to reuse already-interpolated targets) or only interpolate targets when they were not already interpolated by runShardSplitQuery.

advanced-sql-analytics-framework-grafana.texto: WHAT: enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path because both `if enabled { return false }` and the trailing `return false` yield the same value, making the flag check dead code (and `enabled` is the negation of the flag). WHY: SQL expressions can never be parsed via this path no matter how the `sqlExpressions` toggle is configured, so the new gate silently breaks (or never enables) the feature and its name/semantics contradict the flag. HOW: return the negated flag directly, e.g. `if h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions) { return false }; return true`, or remove the helper and gate on `!IsEnabledGlobally`.

WHAT: DB.RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList are stubs that only return `errors.New("not implemented")`, replacing the removed go-duck implementation. WHY: `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:26` (RunCommands) and `pkg/expr/sql_command.go:100` (QueryFramesInto) now always error, so every SQL expression fails at parse time or returns a query error to the client, and the DuckDB SQL/aggregate functionality is silently gone rather than merely gated. HOW: wire the intended execution backend (or, if permanent removal is intended, delete the SQL command path and its API surface instead of returning unimplemented errors at runtime).

WHAT: The new SQL disable check exists only in ReadQuery (reader.go:129, parser path gated by FlagExpressionParser), while NewSQLCommand is still reached unguarded via nodes.go:160 -> UnmarshalSQLCommand. WHY: The non-parser code path constructs and executes SQLCommand regardless of `sqlExpressions`, so the intended disable is not enforced where it matters; additionally a stub/parse failure inside NewSQLCommand (sql.TablesList now always errors) is swallowed into the generic "failed to parse expression" wrap at nodes.go:165, masking the real cause. HOW: enforce the feature-flag check at the single choke point (NewSQLCommand or the nodes.go:159-160 case) so both construction paths respect the toggle.

WHAT: the SQL-disabled branch reports `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"` although the feature is deliberately disabled, not unimplemented. WHY: this string collides with the codebase's genuine "not implemented" signal (e.g. nodes.go:162) and is surfaced to the user via buildCMDNode's wrapper, so operators debugging a rejected SQL expression are told the feature does not exist instead of that it is disabled. HOW: return an explicit disabled message such as `fmt.Errorf("sql expressions are disabled")`.

anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.texto: WHAT: `tagDeviceUI` writes the local-cache entry via `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` (line 87) before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, so when the device limit is reached the cache is already populated while the error is returned. WHY: on the next request for the same device ID, the cache hit at line 83 makes `tagDeviceUI` return nil, `TagDevice` returns nil, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` grants an identity — the newly added `ErrDeviceLimitReached` auth block is silently bypassed for every device that has ever been tagged until the 29-minute cache TTL expires. HOW: only populate the cache after a successful `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (move the `SetDefault` call below the error check), or evict the key on error with `a.localCache.Delete(key)`.

WHAT: The device limit is enforced with a check-then-act sequence — `CountDevices` at line 110 is read, then at line 115 `count >= s.deviceLimit` decides whether to insert a new device, without a transaction, lock, or unique constraint tying the two. WHY: concurrent anonymous requests for distinct device IDs can all observe `count < deviceLimit` and each proceed to the INSERT branch, allowing the number of stored devices to exceed `deviceLimit`; the limit is not a hard cap under load. HOW: perform the count and insert inside a single transaction (e.g. select-for-update or a serializable transaction) or add a schema-level constraint that rejects inserts once the active-device count reaches the limit.

async-import-of-the-appstore-packages-ca.texto: WHAT: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` makes the calendar/video deletion fire-and-forget, and nothing after it awaits the callbacks. WHY: the reschedule mutation returns before `getCalendar(...).deleteEvent(...)` / `deleteMeeting(...)` finish, so the old calendar event can survive the reschedule, and any rejection from the dynamic import or delete becomes an unhandled promise rejection. HOW: collect the promises and await them, e.g. `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`.

WHAT: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` runs the calendar deletion as a fire-and-forget callback with no `await`. WHY: `Reschedule` returns `true` (and sends emails) before `getCalendar(...).deleteEvent(...)` / `deleteMeeting(...)` completes, and since an async callback's rejection does not propagate to the enclosing `try/catch`, deletion failures are silently lost as unhandled rejections. HOW: map to an array of promises and `await Promise.all(...)`.

WHAT: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` runs the calendar deletion as a fire-and-forget callback with no `await`. WHY: `Reschedule` returns `true` (and sends emails) before `getCalendar(...).deleteEvent(...)` / `deleteMeeting(...)` completes, and an async callback's rejection never reaches the enclosing `try/catch`, so failures are silently swallowed as unhandled rejections. HOW: map to an array of promises and `await Promise.all(...)`.

WHAT: the recurring-event branch uses `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`, so the `push` happens after an `await` inside an un-awaited callback. WHY: `apiDeletes` is passed synchronously to `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) before the async callbacks run, so the pushed calendar deletes for the recurring bookings are never awaited and may not be executed before the request returns. HOW: convert to a `for...of` loop (or `await Promise.all(map(...))`) and `await`/collect the delete promises so they are included in the final `Promise.all`.

WHAT: `getCalendar(credential)` is invoked without `await` (or a stored reference) for every credential, but the returned record is only kept when `app.variant === "calendar"`; otherwise the promise is discarded. WHY: since `getCalendar` now starts an async dynamic `import()`, a rejected import for those discarded credentials produces an unhandled promise rejection that can crash the process. HOW: only call `getCalendar` when the app will be included, e.g. `const calendar = app.variant === "calendar" ? getCalendar(credential) : null;` before building the record.

authzservice-improve-authz-caching-grafa.texto: WHAT: A denial computed once from the DB is written to permDenialCache at line 154 and then short-circuits every later Check for that (namespace,user,action,name,parent) to Allowed:false at lines 117-121 for the whole 30s shortCacheTTL, with no invalidation when the user is later granted. WHY: A grant (e.g. a newly-shared dashboard or folder permission) takes up to 30 seconds to take effect, so the user keeps getting denied — the same deny/allow staleness this PR set out to remove for the perm cache, reintroduced on the deny side. HOW: Skip caching a denial when the deny came from a perm-cache read that may be stale, or invalidate the denial entry whenever the underlying permission is granted; at minimum shorten the denial TTL so grants converge quickly.

WHAT: permDenialKey is built from checkReq.UserUID (line 116), while the perm-cache key it is meant to mirror uses the resolved userIdentifiers.UID (line 360); GetUserIdentifiers treats a numeric-looking caller-supplied subject as a user ID, so the same principal can resolve to different key forms. WHY: A denial cached under one identifier form (e.g. numeric ID) is not found when the caller addresses the same user by UID, so the denial cache misses and the DB is re-queried — and when the caller switches forms the two keys diverge, weakening the cache this PR adds. HOW: Resolve the user identifiers once before building permDenialKey and key the denial cache on userIdentifiers.UID for consistency with userPermCacheKey.

comprehensive-workflow-reminder-manageme.texto: WHAT: The workflow-reminder cancellation calls at lines 488 and 490 are invoked inside `forEach` without `await`, and the PR removed the `remindersToDelete` promises that were previously awaited via `Promise.all(...)`. WHY: The handler now returns (and `sendCancelledEmails` fires) before the SendGrid cancel request and the DB `workflowReminder.update/delete` finish; in Next.js serverless runtimes the unawaited promise can be terminated when the response closes, so the reminder may never actually be cancelled — reintroducing the bug this PR fixes. HOW: Collect the returned promises into an array and `await Promise.all(reminderPromises)` before returning, as the previous code did with `remindersToDelete`.

WHAT: At line 968 the previous booking's email reminders are cancelled with `immediateDelete=true`, which in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` posts the SendGrid cancel and `return`s without deleting the row or setting `cancelled`. WHY: No other code deletes the previous booking's `WorkflowReminder` rows in this flow, so rows with `scheduled:true` and `cancelled:null` are orphaned (leaked) until the cron's `scheduledDate <= now` cleanup eventually removes them; the outcome is also inconsistent with the other callsites where the row is cascade-deleted. HOW: Either drop the `immediateDelete` flag so the row is marked `cancelled` and reconciled by the cron, or explicitly delete the reminder row after the SendGrid cancel when `immediateDelete` is set.

WHAT: The `immediateDelete` branch (lines 213-222) performs the SendGrid cancel request and returns without deleting or marking the `WorkflowReminder` row. WHY: Callers that rely on this branch to fully remove a reminder (e.g. handleNewBooking.ts:968) leave the DB row in place with `scheduled:true`/`cancelled:null`, so the reminder record is never cleaned up by this call and the function's contract (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder`) is not honoured. HOW: After the SendGrid cancel, also delete the row (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })`) or set `cancelled:true`, matching the other branches.

database-performance-optimizations-grafa.texto: WHAT: The cleanup ticker interval was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, unconditionally running all cleanup jobs 10x more often. WHY: This increases database and I/O load by an order of magnitude (expired snapshot/version/image deletion, annotation cleanup, query-history pruning, etc.) and is unrelated to the PR's stated goal of avoiding annotation deadlocks on MySQL. HOW: Restore `time.Minute * 10`; if a shorter interval is genuinely required for annotations, make it a configurable setting scoped to the annotation cleanup rather than globally speeding up every job.

WHAT: The new cleanup loop logs at Error level with the full `ids` slice on every successful batch (`"ids", ids`), across all three annotation types and the orphaned-tags pass. WHY: With the default batch size of 100 and configured values up to 32767, each cleanup cycle writes large Error-level log lines listing every ID being deleted, flooding logs and triggering false alerts on a routine success path. HOW: Remove these diagnostic logs or downgrade to Debug and drop the raw `ids` slice; also note the `"err", err` key is always nil here since the error was already returned above.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex.texto: WHAT: `recordStorageDuration` is called with the object `name` in the `kind` label position instead of `options.Kind`. WHY: `metrics.go:59` forwards this argument to the `kind` label of `dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds`, so every mode-3 delete emits a unique bogus `kind` value (the object name), destroying the cardinality and the kind-based aggregation of the metric. HOW: pass `options.Kind` as done by every other call site in this file.

WHAT: The async legacy `DeleteCollection` records its result via `recordStorageDuration` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. WHY: the legacy write latency/error is attributed to `dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds` while `dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds` is never incremented for `delete-collection`, so the legacy health signal for this method is missing and the storage signal is corrupted with a `startLegacy` duration. HOW: use `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`, matching mode1/mode2.

WHAT: `Delete` builds the per-request logger on line 96 but then stores `d.Log` — the un-scoped base logger — into the context on line 97. WHY: the context handed to `d.Storage.Delete` loses the `name`/`kind`/`method` values that every other mode-3 method propagates, so log lines emitted from Storage and its callees cannot be correlated to the request. HOW: install the scoped logger: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`.

WHAT: The async legacy write goroutines discard the returned error — `errObjectSt` is passed only to the metric and never logged, so a failed legacy create/update/delete produces no log line at all. WHY: in mode 3 the legacy write is the safety net for the data, so a silent divergence between unified and legacy storage is invisible in logs and can only be detected via metrics, defeating the purpose of the dual write. HOW: log the error in each goroutine using the scoped `log` (e.g. `log.Error(errObjectSt, "unable to write object in legacy storage")`).

WHAT: `context.WithTimeoutCause` with an `errors.New(...)` cause is used for the legacy write timeouts, but `context.Cause` is never read anywhere in the package, making the cause dead. WHY: the cause string is constructed on every write only to be discarded, and `WithTimeoutCause`/`WithDeadlineCause` are Go 1.21+ APIs, so this silently raises the module's minimum Go version for no runtime benefit. HOW: if the cause is not consumed, use `context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)`; otherwise read `context.Cause(ctx)` in the error path and log it.

WHAT: `TestMode3_Create` calls `assert.NoError(t, err)` and then dereferences the object via `meta.Accessor(obj)`; `assert` does not stop the test, so a nil `obj` yields a nil accessor and `acc.GetResourceVersion()` panics instead of reporting a clean assertion failure. WHY: the error-path test case returns before this line, but any regression that surfaces a non-nil error with a nil object turns a failing assertion into an opaque panic that obscures the real defect. HOW: use `require.NoError(t, err)` and `require.NotNil(t, obj)` before the accessor dereference.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.texto: WHAT: Imported post content is stored with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged so the HTML never passes through PrettyText's sanitization pipeline. WHY: Any `<script>`/event-handler markup in an attacker-influenced RSS/remote article is rendered verbatim by `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb and executes in the embedding third-party page that includes the widget — a stored XSS across origins. HOW: Sanitize imported HTML before storing (e.g. strip script/style and on* attributes with Nokogiri/Rails sanitizer) instead of returning raw verbatim, or restrict raw_html rendering to a trusted allowlist.

WHAT: `i.content`, `i.title`, and `i.link` are taken from simple-rss without a nil/blank guard, and `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when the feed item has no `<content>` (ATOM feeds often use `<summary>` or omit it). WHY: A single malformed entry aborts the entire `rss.items.each` loop, so all remaining items in the feed are silently skipped for that poll. HOW: Guard with `i.content.to_s` (or `next if i.content.blank?`) before calling `scrub`/`unescapeHTML`.

WHAT: `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` is called with a topic_id read from `TopicEmbed`, but the corresponding topic may have been deleted or trashed after the embed row was created. WHY: `TopicView#find_topic` raises `Discourse::NotFound` for a missing topic, so the embed endpoint returns an error page instead of the "start discussion"/loading view whenever `topic_embeds` outlives its topic.
